metadata.system: PEER'S Capstone Automated Web Vulnerability Scanner
metadata.internship_track: Phase 2: Web App Security & Defensive Automation (Capstone Day 30)

findings.title: Server Technology & Version Information Leakage
findings.description: Web server discloses exact vendor and version strings, assisting attacker exploit targeting.
findings.remediation: Disable ServerTokens and expose generic headers (Server: webserver).

findings.title: Missing Essential Security Headers (6 missing)
findings.description: Missing headers: Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. Increases exposure to XSS, Clickjacking, and MIME confusion.
findings.remediation: Configure web server or reverse proxy to inject all 6 mandatory security headers.

findings.title: Non-Standard Administrative Ports Open ([8080])
findings.description: Target exposes open ports [8080] directly to ingress traffic.
findings.remediation: Restrict administrative ports to VPN or internal management subnets via border firewall.

findings.title: Critical Information Disclosure: Exposed Sensitive Files (/.env, /backup.sql, /.git/)
findings.description: Environment credentials, database backup dumps, or source repositories are publicly accessible.
findings.remediation: Block access to dotfiles and SQL dumps via web server configuration.

findings.title: SQL Injection Vulnerability in Search Parameter ('q')
findings.description: Parameter is concatenated directly into SQL queries without parameterization.
findings.remediation: Use prepared statements and ORM parameterized queries.

findings.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Parameter ('q')
findings.description: User input in search parameter is reflected without context-aware HTML entity encoding.
findings.remediation: Implement strict HTML encoding and enforce Content-Security-Policy.
